title: Embeddable session-owned MCP-HTTP + A2A protocol surface (public serveapi package)
execution_environment: Executor is codex:gpt-5.6-sol under `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`. NO GIT WRITES: a linked worktree's .git is a FILE pointing under the main checkout's .git/worktrees/, which the sandbox excludes. The executor NEVER runs git add/commit/branch/push. Instead: on finishing milestone k it copies EVERY file created-or-modified so far in the sprint (CUMULATIVE, full post-milestone content, not a diff) into .snap/M<k>/ preserving relative paths; the CONTROLLER reconstructs one commit per milestone from .snap/M1, .snap/M2, .snap/M3 in the main checkout. .snap/ is scratch and is never committed. NO SOCKETS, NO NETWORK: loopback binds and outbound network are denied. THEREFORE: every new test in this sprint MUST use httptest.NewRecorder() and MUST NOT use httptest.NewServer — I proved the MCP SDK stateless streamable handler is fully exercisable through a bare recorder (GET -> 405 + `Allow: POST`; POST initialize -> 200, Content-Type text/event-stream, correctly SSE-framed), and that internal/apiserver binds ZERO sockets today (13 httptest.NewServer sites exist, ALL 13 in cmd/ailang across 6 files; 0 in internal/apiserver, which uses httptest.NewRecorder in 12 files). Under that rule the executor's verdicts on ALL M1/M2/M3 tests are AUTHORITATIVE, not sandbox-blind. `go test ./...` and `go test ./cmd/ailang` are UNINFORMATIVE UNDER SANDBOX -> executor must NOT report a verdict on them; the controller re-runs them outside the sandbox (verified cheap: `go test ./cmd/ailang` is ok/rc=0 in ~19s in a Claude-agent session, with a positive control binding 127.0.0.1). WORKTREE: /Users/voightkampff/dev/sunholo-data/.wt-iter139-mcp-lane-b — a SIBLING of the repo, NEVER under /tmp: a /tmp-rooted checkout fails TestIsTempPath (internal/loader/loader_test.go:11) and TestSolve_HardTimeout_FakeSolverIgnoringT (internal/smt/solver_timeout_test.go:19) for the LOCATION, producing a red CI can never reproduce. Path verified free at plan time (14 worktrees exist; /private/tmp/wt-iter130-qwen36 is a live example of the anti-pattern). Every wait bounded by a `date +%s` deadline, cap <= 30 min. NOTE: .ailang/ is gitignored but every sibling sprint JSON is TRACKED — commit this file with `git add -f .ailang/state/sprints/sprint_M-MCP-EXACT-TOOL-SURFACE-LANE-B.json`.
executor_constraints: FORBIDDEN: httptest.NewServer in any new test (would be uninformative by construction under the sandbox). Use httptest.NewRecorder().

FORBIDDEN: any new implementation in internal/apiserver/server.go. It is 764 lines and the gate at make/code-health.mk:127 fires at >800, leaving 36 lines. The only permitted change there is the single isExposed call site at :686 (net 0 lines).
FORBIDDEN: reporting a pass/fail verdict for `go test ./...` or `go test ./cmd/ailang` from inside the sandbox. Flag them for controller re-run.
FORBIDDEN: git add / git commit / git branch / git push. Use the .snap/M<k>/ cumulative snapshot protocol.
MANDATORY: internal/apiserver must NEVER import ailang/serveapi (would be an import cycle). Verified 0 today, control internal/embed = 1.
MANDATORY: the embedded MCP handler constructs mcp.StreamableHTTPOptions{Stateless: true}. Frozen by the design doc; also already the standalone default at internal/apiserver/mcp.go:305.

metadata.scope: Add one narrow PUBLIC Go package `serveapi` (import path github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/serveapi) that mounts AILANG-owned MCP-HTTP and A2A handlers on a caller-owned http.ServeMux and projects exactly one host-supplied, request-session-specific tool set into BOTH protocols. Three parts: (1) the public contract (SessionResolver / ToolSource / Invoker / ToolDescriptor / Config with CallbackTimeout + MaxConcurrentCallbacks) plus a protocol-neutral request-local AuthorizedSurface gateway and a bounded-callback runner (per-call deadline + capacity semaphore held until the callback goroutine EXITS + buffered-channel select); (2) a request-scoped MCP adapter that resolves in an OUTER wrapper handler, writes frozen JSON-RPC error envelopes itself, and delegates success to a pre-built SDK stateless StreamableHTTPHandler whose getServer(req) only reads the already-computed surface out of the request context; (3) the A2A card+task projection, Mount, the generalization of isExposed into the shared gateway, rules/docs updates, and the gate sweep.
metadata.non_scope: No World persistence, stores, schedulers, queues, task state, or session storage. No authentication policy, token parsing, principal models, capability computation, or revocation storage — the host supplies all of that behind callbacks. No redesign of Lane A: --no-feedback-tool stays default-false and the standalone CLI stays on apiserver.New / Server.Start and is NOT routed through serveapi.New. No dynamic REST/OpenAPI endpoints generated from caller descriptors. No replacing the MCP Go SDK, no hand-written SSE, no change to upstream MCP/A2A wire semantics. No public exposure of internal/apiserver.Server, ExportInfo, the compiler engine, or the effect context. No stateful/resumable MCP sessions or EventStore stream resumption. Do NOT fold @nomcp into the protocol-neutral gateway (it is deliberately MCP-only; folding it would silently hide those exports from A2A and OpenAPI too).
planner_refutations_and_new_hazards: REFUTED — `make check-file-sizes` CANNOT see serveapi/. The gate body is `for file in $(find internal cmd -name "*.go")` (make/code-health.mk:127-131); it never walks a top-level directory. Positive control: that find returns 45 files under internal/apiserver/ and 0 under runtime/+std/ even though 6 .go files exist there. So the doc's M3 AC crediting check-file-sizes for the new package is VACUOUS. Plan adds an explicit `wc -l serveapi/*.go` table.

REFUTED — `make check-boundaries` CANNOT see serveapi/ either. scripts/check_boundaries.sh iterates only internal/<pkg> for CORE_PKGS=(parser types eval core elaborate effects builtins lexer ast pipeline runtime link iface) and DASHBOARD_PKGS=(server coordinator observatory messaging); `apiserver` is in NEITHER (grep count 0; positive control `parser` = 1) and no top-level dir is ever scanned. The gate passes IDENTICALLY whether or not serveapi imports the compiler core. The doc's M3 AC and its 'Public package layering' Conflict Surface row are therefore NOT DISCRIMINATING. Replaced by a two-sided `go list` import assertion (M1 AC2).

REFUTED (scope-qualified) — the doc's V19 says `go test ./cmd/ailang` panics with `bind: operation not permitted` and is UNINFORMATIVE. In a Claude-agent session it is rc=0, `ok ... 19.282s`, with ZERO bind errors, and a positive control bound a real listener at http://127.0.0.1:62979. Both are true — the designer measured the codex sandbox, I measured a Claude-agent session. The useful consequence: the controller CAN re-run every loopback-dependent suite for ~20s, so 'controller re-runs outside sandbox' is a real step, not a deferred hope.

NEW CRITICAL HAZARD — mcp.Server.AddTool PANICS (does not error) on host-supplied schemas, and on the embedded path it runs INSIDE an HTTP handler goroutine, per request, on ARBITRARY host data. Reproduced: nil InputSchema -> `panic: AddTool "bad2": missing input schema`; scalar InputSchema -> `panic: AddTool "bad": can't marshal input schema to a JSON object`. It also panics on type != "object", on an unmarshalable OutputSchema, and on invalid param-header annotations, while validateToolName only LOGS (s.opts.Logger.Error) so a bad NAME registers silently. The doc's ToolDescriptor makes InputSchema an ordinary optional field, so an omitting host crashes the handler; net/http recovers per-connection and aborts, giving a truncated response rather than the doc's 'explicit constructor/request error'. Gateway MUST reject nil AND non-object AND bad names BEFORE any AddTool, returning errors and never silently defaulting. The doc's M1 AC only covers 'a scalar input schema' — a NIL-schema case is added, plus an M2 panic-safety AC.

NEW — the doc CONTRADICTS ITSELF on where resolution happens, and only one option can emit the frozen envelope. Overview says the embedded FACTORY resolves and returns a fresh SDK server (i.e. inside getServer(req)); Bounded Host Callbacks says the timeout envelope is emitted BEFORE handing control to the SDK. Only the second is implementable: I measured that getServer returning nil yields HTTP 400, Content-Type text/plain, body `no server available` — the SDK's ONLY failure channel from that hook. It structurally cannot produce -32603 / 'host callback timed out' / HTTP 200 / application/json, and cannot echo the JSON-RPC id. The plan PINS the wrapper architecture in the M2 preamble to remove a 2-4h executor rewrite. Also: the wrapper's body read precedes the SDK's own http.MaxBytesReader (streamable.go:344-345), so the wrapper must impose its own cap — reuse mcp.DefaultMaxRequestBodyBytes (4<<20).

NEW — @nomcp is ALREADY a second, MCP-only filter, so the invariant M3 is told to restate is false as written. .claude/rules/api-server.md:31 claims isExposed() is 'the single filtering point... No additional filtering logic should be added in individual consumers', but internal/apiserver/mcp.go:94-95 does `if export.IsNoMCP { continue }`, deliberately (server.go:146: 'hide from the MCP tool surface only (HTTP/OpenAPI/A2A unaffected)'). An executor taking the restated invariant literally would fold @nomcp into the protocol-neutral gateway and silently hide those exports from A2A and OpenAPI. The rule rewrite must NAME @nomcp as the one sanctioned protocol-scoped, annotation-declared narrowing, distinct from AUTHORITY filtering. Separately, the rule file's frontmatter `paths:` is internal/apiserver/** and cmd/ailang/serve_api.go — it MUST gain serveapi/**, or the newly-written invariant never loads for an agent editing the new package.

NEW — the external-module compile fixture (M1's flagship AC) has TWO offline gotchas, both now proven and solved. (1) The fixture go.mod MUST declare `go 1.26.5` matching the replace target; with `go 1.24` it fails `go: module ... requires go >= 1.26.5 (running go 1.26.4)`, an error that looks nothing like an import problem. (2) It MUST `cp <worktree>/go.sum .`, or transitive external deps (MCP SDK, jsonschema-go, ...) have no sums and GOPROXY=off cannot invent them. Verified recipe rc=0 offline, and the denial half returns the EXACT string the doc demands: `use of internal package github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/internal/apiserver not allowed`. The replace must point at the WORKTREE, not the main checkout.

CONFIRMED by re-measurement (doc premises that held): server.go = 764 lines with the gate at 800 (36 lines headroom); serveapi/ genuinely absent (control runtime/ present); module path github.com/sunholo-data/ailang; apiserver.Config has 15 fields (doc's refutation of '16' is right) and New returns *Server with no error; mcp.go:303-306 hands us a per-request *http.Request and DISCARDS it while already setting Stateless: true; mcp.Tool has both `InputSchema any` and `OutputSchema any`, both documented to accept json.RawMessage, so the doc's OutputSchema projection is feasible; A2A errors are HTTP 200 + JSON-RPC (a2a.go:304 `w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) // JSON-RPC always returns 200.`, codes -32600/-32601/-32602, no StatusInternalServerError on the task path) and -32603 is unused there (count 0, control -32602 = 6); 6 production isExposed call sites at handler.go:142, server.go:686, a2a.go:57, a2a.go:185, openapi.go:187, mcp.go:91 (28 total refs including tests); both make targets exist (1 each); .claude/rules/api-server.md is 46 lines and docs/docs/guides/serve-api.md is 1384 lines.
metadata.ordering_change_from_design_doc: CHANGED, in two ways, both recorded because the doc's own ordering is not bisectable. (a) AC RE-ASSIGNMENT: THREE of the doc's six M1 ACs are UNSATISFIABLE AT THE M1 BOUNDARY because they require HTTP handlers that only arrive in M2 (MCP) and M3 (A2A) — M1 AC2 (pointer-sentinel session through a request), M1 AC5 (the 20ms/250ms timeout table, whose own text says 'the same table covers MCP POST, A2A task POST, and A2A card GET'), and M1 AC6 (bounded concurrency, whose overload envelope is 'HTTP 200 on MCP/A2A POST; HTTP 503 on A2A card GET'). This is the exact class that invalidated iteration 135's patch evidence. Resolution: the callback runner becomes a protocol-neutral directly-unit-testable unit, so M1 keeps the STRONGER runner-level halves (observed context deadline, callback STARTS capped at N, token held until goroutine exit, goroutine-count growth) and the WIRE halves move to the milestone that first provides that transport. Nothing is dropped or weakened. (b) WORK MOVE: the loaded-export isExposed -> gateway generalization moves M1 -> M3, because the embedded path NEVER calls it (embedded authorization is callerSurface([]ToolDescriptor)), so M1/M2 have zero dependency on it; and because it is the ONLY change in the sprint that can regress standalone behavior across 6 production call sites in 5 files, so landing it LAST keeps the bisect boundary sharp — if standalone tests go red, exactly one commit is suspect. M1 still defines AuthorizedSurface and callerSurface (what M2 consumes); only loadedExportSurface and the 6 call-site rewires move.
metadata.budget_verdict: The design doc's ~17h / 3-milestone budget is WRONG — LOW BY ROUGHLY 1.5x. Realistic: ~25h over 3.5 executor days. Four reasons: (1) the doc's own AC set is the cost driver, not LOC — an offline cross-module compile fixture, a 3x3 timeout table, a goroutine-accounting concurrency test, frozen wire envelopes across 5 error classes x 3 entry points (15 assertions each with explicit NEGATIVE clauses), a 100-request interleaved race test, and two-sided exact-set assertions in both protocols, giving test LOC ~= 70% of implementation LOC rather than the usual 30-50%; (2) the resolution-location contradiction is a real 2-4h fork this plan removes by pinning, but the pinning was never in the 17h; (3) same-subsystem calibration — Lane A (aa02f0d9f) landed 1023 insertions of which 534 was its sprint plan, so ~490 LOC of code+tests+docs for a FAR smaller scope (one flag, one conditional, one dispatch check), while Lane B is ~1450 LOC across a new public package, a new protocol-neutral authorization type, a concurrency-bounded callback runtime, and two protocol adapters; (4) recent comparable sprints — M-RECORDED-STREAM-API-S1 730 LOC/3.75d, M-EVAL-STANDARD-CONFIDENCE-GATING 460 LOC/4d. RECOMMENDATION: accept ~25h / 3.5d and keep all three milestones; do NOT cut any AC. If a hard 3-day box is required, the ONLY clean cut is deferring M3's isExposed generalization to a follow-up sprint (~3.5h, the one block with no embedded-path dependency), accepting that the rule file temporarily describes behavior the code does not yet have.

features.description: Create the public `serveapi` package (serveapi/serveapi.go ~200 LOC: Session/SessionResolver/ToolSource/Invoker/ToolDescriptor/Invocation/InvocationResult/Config/AgentInfo, DefaultCallbackTimeout=5s, DefaultMaxConcurrentCallbacks=64, New with validation rejecting nil callbacks, invalid agent metadata, negative CallbackTimeout and negative MaxConcurrentCallbacks; stdlib types ONLY, no internal types leaked). MCPHandler()/A2AHandler()/Mount() are DECLARED at M1 so the external compile fixture is real; their wire behavior completes in M2/M3. Add internal/apiserver/authorized_surface.go (~190 LOC): the protocol-neutral request-local gateway with callerSurface([]internalDescriptorDTO) doing deep-copy (slice + nested json.RawMessage + Tags + Examples) -> validate -> sort-by-name -> immutable AuthorizedSurface with Lookup(name) and All(). Validation is FAIL-LOUD and MUST run BEFORE any mcp.Server.AddTool because AddTool PANICS rather than errors: reject nil InputSchema, reject non-object InputSchema, reject an unmarshalable OutputSchema, reject duplicate names, reject names failing AILANG's stricter ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ via validateMCPName (the SDK's own validateToolName only LOGS a bad name). NEVER silently default a nil schema to {"type":"object"} — CLAUDE.md rule 2 forbids silent fallbacks on data-integrity paths. Add internal/apiserver/callbacks.go (~150 LOC): the bounded-callback runner used by BOTH protocols — derives a child context whose deadline is the EARLIER of the incoming request deadline and now+CallbackTimeout, acquires a capacity token BEFORE launching the callback goroutine and holds it until that goroutine ACTUALLY EXITS (not until the handler stops waiting), runs the callback behind a ONE-RESULT BUFFERED channel, and selects between result and ctx.Done(). Zero CallbackTimeout selects DefaultCallbackTimeout, never 'wait forever'. Plus authorized_surface_test.go (~180) and callbacks_test.go (~200). NOTE: the design doc did not enumerate callbacks.go as a file; it is added here so the runner is protocol-neutral and directly unit-testable, which is what makes M1 independently verifiable. serveapi/*.go is NOT covered by make check-file-sizes (the gate is `find internal cmd`), so its size is asserted explicitly instead.
acceptance_criteria: AC1.1 (-> doc M1 AC1) EXTERNAL-MODULE FIXTURE, OFFLINE, RECIPE PROVEN BY THE PLANNER. In a scratch dir INSIDE the worktree (e.g. <worktree>/.snap-scratch/extfixture/, NOT /tmp — workspace-write may deny writes outside the workspace): a go.mod declaring `go 1.26.5` (NOT 1.24 — with 1.24 it fails `go: module ... requires go >= 1.26.5 (running go 1.26.4)`, an error that looks nothing like an import problem), `require github.com/sunholo-data/ailang v0.0.0`, `replace github.com/sunholo-data/ailang => /Users/voightkampff/dev/sunholo-data/.wt-iter139-mcp-lane-b` (the WORKTREE, not the main checkout), plus `cp <worktree>/go.sum .` (without it, transitive deps like the MCP SDK and jsonschema-go have no sums and GOPROXY=off cannot invent them). Then `GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off go build ./...` must be rc=0 for a file importing github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/serveapi that calls serveapi.New with sentinel callbacks and then MCPHandler(), A2AHandler(), and Mount(mux). In the SAME fixture, a `//go:build denied` file importing internal/apiserver must fail with EXACTLY `use of internal package github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/internal/apiserver not allowed`. DISCRIMINATING BOTH WAYS: the two halves are opposite-signed, and the positive half is what proves the toolchain/go.sum setup is not silently broken — a fixture that fails to build for setup reasons would otherwise make the denial half pass vacuously.

AC1.2 (NEW, replaces the doc's vacuous make check-boundaries credit) IMPORT DIRECTION, TWO-SIDED, WITH INSTRUMENT-FAILURE GUARD. `go list -f '{{join .Imports "\n"}}' ./serveapi` must contain ZERO of internal/(parser|types|eval|core|elaborate|pipeline) AND AT LEAST ONE internal/apiserver; print both counts side by side and t.Fatal("instrument failure") if the internal/apiserver count is 0 rather than passing on an empty result set. Symmetric: `go list -f '{{join .Imports "\n"}}' ./internal/apiserver` must contain ZERO ailang/serveapi (no import cycle), with internal/embed as the known-positive control (measured = 1 at plan time). THIS IS THE REAL LAYERING EVIDENCE: make check-boundaries CANNOT see either package — scripts/check_boundaries.sh only iterates internal/<pkg> for CORE_PKGS and DASHBOARD_PKGS, `apiserver` is in neither (grep count 0, control `parser` = 1), and no top-level dir is ever scanned, so that gate passes identically whether or not serveapi imports the compiler core.

AC1.3 (-> doc M1 AC3, STRENGTHENED with the nil case) DESCRIPTOR GATEWAY TABLE. Input [zeta, alpha] -> surface order [alpha, zeta]. Duplicate `alpha` -> error. Scalar InputSchema -> error. NIL InputSchema -> error (NEW: mcp.Server.AddTool would otherwise `panic: AddTool "x": missing input schema`; the doc's AC covered only the scalar case). OutputSchema that fails to marshal -> error. Name failing ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ -> error. Every case RETURNS an error — never panics, never silently defaults. DEEP-COPY PROOF: mutate the caller's slice, the nested json.RawMessage bytes, Tags, and Examples AFTER Tools returns, then assert the served surface is byte-identical to the pre-mutation snapshot. DISCRIMINATING: the mutation half fails on a shallow copy; the nil/scalar halves fail as a MISSING ERROR if validation is skipped (the SDK panic only manifests at M2, so a skipped check here cannot hide behind a crash).

AC1.4 (-> doc M1 AC5, RUNNER HALF — the wire halves move to M2/M3) TIMEOUT SELECTION AND BOUND, NO HTTP. CallbackTimeout: 20*time.Millisecond with a callback that NEVER returns -> the runner returns an error matching context.DeadlineExceeded after AT LEAST 20ms and BEFORE a 250ms outer deadline, and the NEXT callback in the chain is never entered (counter == 0). CallbackTimeout: 0 -> the effective deadline is DefaultCallbackTimeout, asserted by READING THE DEADLINE OFF THE CONTEXT handed to the callback and requiring it in (now+4s, now+6s) — deliberately NOT by asserting 5s == DefaultCallbackTimeout, which would be a test parameterized on the very constant it guards (the vacuous-AC class this mission has already shipped four times). Negative CallbackTimeout -> New returns an error. A fast callback with CallbackTimeout: 0 succeeds. DISCRIMINATING: the observed-deadline window FAILS if zero is treated as 'no deadline at all' and FAILS if the configured duration is ignored.

AC1.5 (-> doc M1 AC6, ACCOUNTING HALF) BOUNDED CONCURRENCY. MaxConcurrentCallbacks: 4 plus a callback that blocks PERMANENTLY. Launch 40 runner calls. Assert (a) callback STARTS == 4 exactly — call 5 never enters the callback; (b) calls 5..40 each return the overload sentinel WITHOUT entering the callback; (c) runtime.NumGoroutine() sampled after the burst does not GROW WITH CALL COUNT — compare the 40-call and 80-call figures and require the difference <= a small constant (comparing growth, not an absolute number, so the assertion is not flaky). Then release the blocked callbacks and assert capacity RECOVERS. CONTROL: 40 FAST calls at the same MaxConcurrentCallbacks: 4 produce ZERO overload errors. DISCRIMINATING IN THREE DIRECTIONS: no semaphore -> starts grow with call count; token released when the handler stops waiting instead of when the goroutine exits -> capacity recovers and starts exceed 4; a cap that simply rejects everything -> the fast-call control fails.

AC1.6 GATES, NARROWING RECORDED. `gofmt -l` over the changed files prints nothing (report the `| wc -l` count beside it, since an empty output is otherwise indistinguishable from a broken command); `go vet ./serveapi ./internal/apiserver` rc=0; `go test ./internal/apiserver ./serveapi` rc=0 with rc captured via a file, NOT through a pipe (`cmd > /tmp/out 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"` — exit codes through pipes report the LAST command's status, and ${PIPESTATUS[0]} is bash-only and silently EMPTY under zsh). THIS IS NOT `go test ./...`; the narrowing travels with the finding.

AC1.7 SNAPSHOT. .snap/M1/ contains the cumulative full post-milestone content of all six files above, at their repo-relative paths. Verify by `find .snap/M1 -type f | wc -l` == 6 and by diffing each against its worktree copy (must be identical).
features.notes: Landed on dev before M3 execution: public contract, authorized surface, and bounded callback runner.

features.description: Add internal/apiserver/embedded_mcp.go (~260 LOC) implementing the request-scoped MCP adapter. ARCHITECTURE IS PINNED BY THE SPRINT PLAN — DO NOT RE-LITIGATE IT. The design doc contradicts itself: its Overview says the embedded FACTORY resolves the request and returns a fresh SDK server (i.e. inside getServer(req)), while its Bounded Host Callbacks section says the timeout envelope is emitted BEFORE handing control to the SDK. Only the second is implementable: the planner measured that getServer returning nil yields HTTP 400, Content-Type text/plain, body `no server available` — the SDK's ONLY failure channel from that hook — so it structurally cannot produce -32603 / 'host callback timed out' / HTTP 200 / application/json and cannot echo the JSON-RPC id. THEREFORE MCPHandler() returns a WRAPPER http.Handler whose order is: bounded-read the body (cap mcp.DefaultMaxRequestBodyBytes = 4<<20, because the wrapper reads BEFORE the SDK installs its own http.MaxBytesReader at streamable.go:344-345) -> restore via io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(buf)) -> best-effort decode the JSON-RPC id -> ResolveSession -> Tools -> callerSurface gateway -> ON FAILURE write the frozen envelope directly and RETURN WITHOUT TOUCHING THE SDK -> ON SUCCESS stash AuthorizedSurface + session in the request context and delegate to a StreamableHTTPHandler BUILT ONCE AT New whose getServer(req) merely reads them back and constructs the per-request *mcp.Server. StreamableHTTPOptions{Stateless: true} is mandatory and frozen. Registration must be PANIC-SAFE: AddTool panics on nil/non-object InputSchema, unmarshalable OutputSchema, and invalid param-header annotations, so the M1 gateway validation is load-bearing and the adapter must additionally not leave poisoned state if one descriptor is bad. Reuse mcpError() (internal/apiserver/mcp.go:379) and validateMCPName() (mcp_schema.go:103); do NOT reuse makeToolHandler — it is engine-coupled (ms.server.engine.CallPreserveFloats + embed.ToGo) and the embedded path takes json.RawMessage in and out. mcp.go shrinks slightly (386 -> ~370) via extraction; standalone construction semantics are UNCHANGED. Also wire serveapi.MCPHandler() to the adapter. Tests go in embedded_mcp_test.go (~330) — the design doc's single ~350 LOC embedded_test.go is split AT SOURCE into per-protocol files so neither approaches the 800-line gate.
acceptance_criteria: AC2.1 (-> doc M2 AC1) EXACT A/B SURFACES. MCP tools/list as principal A is EXACTLY [alpha_only, shared]; as B EXACTLY [beta_only, shared]. Assert SET EQUALITY in both directions (not Contains) and explicitly assert the FOREIGN sentinel is ABSENT. An empty tool list must t.Fatal("instrument failure") rather than pass — an absence claim needs the known-positive `shared` in the same response as its control.

AC2.2 (-> doc M2 AC2) DISPATCH AUTHORIZATION + POINTER SESSION IDENTITY. Calling alpha_only as A: invocation counter == 1, Invoke received the sessionA POINTER (== on the sentinel pointer, with a DISTINCT sessionB pointer live in the same test so a stuck-value or swapped-session bug is caught), arguments byte-equal {"nonce":"A-137"}. Calling alpha_only as B: MCP unknown-tool error and the invocation counter STAYS 0. DISCRIMINATING: fails on a zero, stringified, copied, or swapped session, and fails if dispatch reaches Invoke for an unauthorized name.

AC2.3 (-> doc M2 AC3) submit_feedback IS NOT AMBIENT. With an EMPTY descriptor set, tools/list returns 0 tools and does not contain submit_feedback. The SAME test function then supplies an explicit submit_feedback descriptor and asserts it appears and dispatches through the host Invoker — the non-empty half is the known-positive control that keeps the zero-result half from passing on a broken handler. Assert the embedded constructor NEVER calls registerFeedbackTool: `grep -c registerFeedbackTool internal/apiserver/embedded_mcp.go` == 0 with the known-positive control `grep -c registerFeedbackTool internal/apiserver/mcp.go` > 0 in the same command.

AC2.4 (-> doc M2 AC5) STATELESS TRANSPORT, RECORDER ONLY. httptest.NewRecorder GET to /mcp/ -> 405 with header `Allow: POST` and body `Method Not Allowed`. A correctly headed POST (Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json, text/event-stream) reaches the request-local server and returns its sentinel tool, with Content-Type text/event-stream and an `event: message` line. The planner verified ALL of this is reachable through a bare recorder with no socket. DISCRIMINATING: stateful mode routes GET into serveStateful, which does NOT return 405 — so this fails if Stateless is ever flipped or the SDK dispatch is bypassed.

AC2.5 (NEW — the AddTool panic hazard) PANIC SAFETY AT PER-REQUEST REGISTRATION. A host returning a descriptor with nil InputSchema, and one with InputSchema `"scalar"`, must EACH produce the frozen protocol error envelope with the invocation counter at 0, AND the test must prove the process did not panic: the recorder body must be a DECODABLE envelope (not a truncated/aborted connection), and a SUBSEQUENT good request on the SAME handler must still succeed, proving no poisoned state. Control: the same handler with a valid descriptor returns 200. DISCRIMINATING: with validation removed, AddTool panics (reproduced by the planner: `panic: AddTool "bad2": missing input schema` and `panic: AddTool "bad": can't marshal input schema to a JSON object`), net/http recovers per-connection and aborts, so the recorder body is not a decodable envelope and the follow-up assertion catches poisoned state.

AC2.6 (-> doc M1 AC5, MCP WIRE HALF) FROZEN MCP TIMEOUT ENVELOPE. CallbackTimeout: 20*time.Millisecond; three table cases installing a NON-RETURNING ResolveSession, Tools, and Invoke. Each must yield: HTTP 200, Content-Type application/json, JSON-RPC error.code == -32603, error.message == "host callback timed out", the id ECHOED when decodable and `null` when not (two sub-cases), elapsed >= 20ms and < a 250ms outer test deadline, and the next-callback counter == 0. Plus a callback returning context.Canceled -> "host callback canceled". Plus a resolver authorization error -> 401/403 per the typed contract. EXPLICITLY assert the response is NOT 500 and NOT 504 (the doc forbids turning MCP callback timeouts into HTTP 500/504). DISCRIMINATING: this test HANGS past its outer deadline if handler-side timeout selection is absent, and fails on wrong-envelope assertions if the configured duration or protocol mapping is not wired.

AC2.7 (-> doc M1 AC6, MCP WIRE HALF) OVERLOAD ENVELOPE. MaxConcurrentCallbacks: 4 plus a permanently blocking callback; send 40 POSTs. Excess requests return HTTP 200, -32603, "host callback capacity exceeded", WITHOUT entering the callback. CONTROL: 40 FAST POSTs at the same N produce ZERO overload envelopes, proving the cap is not simply rejecting everything.

AC2.8 (-> doc M2 AC4) STANDALONE MCP REGRESSIONS UNCHANGED. `go test ./internal/apiserver` rc=0 with protocol_test.go (14 Test funcs), mcp_schema_test.go (9), feedback_tool_surface_test.go (4), nomcp_test.go (5), filtering_test.go (8), a2a_dispatch_gate_test.go (2) all still EXECUTING — proven by listing the run test NAMES (`-v` and grep `^--- PASS`), not by an aggregate `ok` line, which would also print if the tests had been deleted. NO hand-written SSE encoder is introduced: `grep -c 'event: message' internal/apiserver/*.go` over non-test files == 0, with the SDK's own mcp/streamable.go as the known-positive control that the pattern matches at all.

acceptance_criteria: AC3.1 (-> doc M3 AC1) A2A CARD EXACT SETS. Using the SAME A/B descriptor callbacks as M2: the card as A exposes EXACTLY [alpha_only, shared] and as B EXACTLY [beta_only, shared]; set equality in both directions plus explicit foreign-sentinel absence. Descriptions, tags, and examples must be byte-equal to the source descriptors using NON-DEFAULT SENTINEL VALUES for each (empty tags/examples would make the equality assertion vacuous). Both `id` and `name` equal the descriptor name. This catches a separate A2A enumeration path drifting from the MCP one.

AC3.2 (-> doc M3 AC2) A2A DISPATCH AUTHORIZATION. A2A send of beta_only as B -> invocation counter 1 with the sessionB POINTER. The same send as A -> JSON-RPC -32602 invalid-params and the counter STAYS 0.

AC3.3 (-> doc M3 AC3) MOUNT, RECORDER ONLY, NO SOCKET. One http.ServeMux, api.Mount(mux), then via httptest.NewRecorder: MCP initialize at /mcp/ returns 200 with Content-Type text/event-stream; an agent card at /.well-known/agent.json; A2A JSON-RPC at /a2a/. Prove no socket is bound BY CONSTRUCTION: `grep -c httptest.NewServer` over the new test files == 0, with the SDK's or cmd/ailang's usage as the known-positive control that the pattern matches at all (13 sites exist in cmd/ailang). Also assert StripPrefix behavior for /mcp (no trailing slash) and /mcp/deep/path.

AC3.4 (-> doc M1 AC5/AC6, A2A WIRE HALF) FROZEN A2A ENVELOPES, EACH ASSERTING THE OTHER MAPPING WAS NOT USED. Task POST timeout -> HTTP 200, -32603, "host callback timed out". Card GET timeout -> HTTP 504 with the same message in a JSON body. Card GET overload -> HTTP 503, "host callback capacity exceeded". Task POST overload -> HTTP 200 + -32603. Canceled -> "host callback canceled", POST 200 / card GET 500. Each case asserts the expected code AND that the other protocol's mapping was NOT used (e.g. card GET timeout is 504, explicitly NOT 200 and NOT 503). These mappings preserve the EXISTING A2A wire format, verified not assumed: a2a.go:304 is `w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK) // JSON-RPC always returns 200.` and every existing task error is a JSON-RPC code (-32600 at :127, -32601 at :137, -32602 at :145/158/166/178/190/267 = 6 sites), with no StatusInternalServerError on the task path; -32603 is NEW to this file (count 0, control -32602 = 6).

AC3.5 (-> doc M1 AC4, MOVED HERE WITH THE REFACTOR) EXPOSURE GENERALIZATION IS NOT VACUOUS. After rewiring all 6 production isExposed call sites: filtering_test.go (8 Test funcs), nomcp_test.go (5), and mcp_schema_test.go (9) pass UNCHANGED — no edits to those three files, proven by showing those paths absent from the set of modified files (via .snap comparison, since the executor cannot run git). THEN the discriminating addition: a table asserting @noexpose hides an export, --routes-only hides a non-@route export, and @nomcp hides from MCP WHILE REMAINING PRESENT IN THE A2A CARD AND OPENAPI. That last clause is the whole point — it is what catches folding @nomcp into the protocol-neutral gateway. DISCRIMINATING: if the refactor made the central gate always-true, every hide-case fails; if @nomcp were folded in, the A2A/OpenAPI presence clauses fail.

AC3.6 (NEW) THE RULE FILE IS ACTUALLY REACHABLE. .claude/rules/api-server.md frontmatter `paths:` includes serveapi/**, asserted by grep with internal/apiserver/** as the known-positive control IN THE SAME COMMAND (it is present today; serveapi/** is not). The Endpoint Filtering section names @nomcp as the single sanctioned protocol-scoped narrowing, distinct from authority filtering. Without the paths change the newly-written invariant never loads for an agent editing the new package — the rule would be true and invisible.

AC3.7 (-> doc M3 AC4) STANDALONE CLI COMPATIBILITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS IN ONE TEST. The default server MCP surface includes BOTH `status` AND `submit_feedback`; with NoFeedbackTool: true it includes `status` and EXCLUDES `submit_feedback`. `status` is the known-positive control that keeps the exclusion half from passing on an empty surface. Also confirm cmd/ailang/serve_api.go still builds apiserver.Config, calls apiserver.New, LoadModules, and srv.Start, and is NOT routed through serveapi.New (grep the call sites).
